verdict.rationale: Mistral documents an include_blocks option that returns paragraph-level blocks with structural block labels and content in reading order. It also extracts headers and footers into separate fields, and a community tester reports good PDF-to-markdown output. However, no evidence explicitly confirms heading levels or nested section hierarchy, and one hands-on report saw a whole page returned as a single image instead of structured text. missing for 10: explicit documentation of heading levels and nested section hierarchy in the output, independent corroboration that structure is preserved consistently across document types.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, parsed output preserves document hierarchy — headings, sections, reading order — so downstream LLMs see structure, not soup

citations.quote: When enabled, each page contains a `blocks` array with paragraph-level bounding boxes, structural block labels, and extracted content in reading order.
When you use them, the response includes header and footer content in the `header` and `footer` fields.
Mistral OCR excels in understanding complex document elements, including interleaved imagery, mathematical expressions, tables, and advanced layouts such as LaTeX
